verdict: Henry Schein grew sales 4% to $3.5 billion and GAAP profit per share jumped 26% to $1.06, helped by strong dental merchandise sales — and by a tariff-refund windfall worth $0.19 a share.

segments.name: Global Distribution & Value-Added Services
segments.note: Delivering dental and medical supplies to practices, plus support services. Shown after $45M of eliminations between Henry Schein's own businesses (gross segment sales $2,944M); dental merchandise sales rose 7.0%.

segments.name: Global Specialty Products
segments.note: Implants, orthodontics and other specialty products made by Henry Schein itself — growth included 2.6 points from acquisitions.

segments.name: Global Technology
segments.note: Practice-management software and tech services for dentists and doctors.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Sales teams, distribution network staff and running the company.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Wear-and-tear on warehouses, systems and acquired intangibles.

opex.name: Restructuring & related costs
opex.note: Costs of the company's restructuring program.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $42M, partly offset by $9M of interest income; plus $3M of equity earnings from part-owned affiliates, added after tax — net −$30M in total.
footerNote: Net income of $126M is the total; $119M was attributable to Henry Schein, Inc. after $7M attributable to noncontrolling interests.

takeaways.title: Dental merchandise led
takeaways.text: Global dental distribution merchandise sales rose 7.0% (5.1% internal growth) — dentists are buying supplies again, and equipment sales also grew 2.3%.

takeaways.title: A tariff-refund boost
takeaways.text: GAAP and non-GAAP results both include a $0.19-per-share net benefit from tariff refunds. Excluding it (and last year's remeasurement gain), non-GAAP EPS still rose 19% to $1.37.

takeaways.title: Margins inched up
takeaways.text: Adjusted EBITDA rose to $321 million and its margin widened 40 basis points to 9.24% — slow, steady operating leverage in a distribution business where thin margins are normal.

oneTimers: The quarter includes a $0.19-per-share net benefit from tariff refunds in both GAAP and non-GAAP results; the year-ago quarter included a $0.23-per-share remeasurement gain.
Restructuring and related costs of $22M are inside GAAP operating expenses; non-GAAP net income was $175M ($1.56 per share) after removing restructuring, amortization and similar items.
